# HyprlandConfigWriter

> **File:** `services/HyprlandConfigWriter.qml` · **Docs:** see [docs/dev](../../README.md)

section's options, loading ~/.config/hypr/user/*.lua after it Also what only Hyprland has: the managed takeover (HyprlandTakeover) and moving the user's binds into axiom (HyprlandBindMerge).

### Properties

- `skippedKeys` (readonly alias): Configured keys the runtime layer skipped because Hyprland's config already binds them
- `configDir` (readonly string)
- `includePath` (readonly string)
- `managedPath` (readonly string)
- `userDir` (readonly string)
- `userFiles` (readonly string): Where the user's own config goes in managed mode
- `includeLines` (readonly string): What the user's hyprland.lua needs for the included mode
- `autostartLines` (readonly string): What a hyprland.lua needs to start axiom with Hyprland, for the detached and included modes (managed starts it itself).
- `includeTarget` (readonly var): The lines above as integration_hookup.py targets in the user's hyprland.lua (IntegrationHookupManager's "compositorInclude" and "compositorAutostart"): the include goes first, so what follows overrid…
- `autostartTarget` (readonly var)
- `shellCommand` (readonly string): How Hyprland and its binds start or call axiom (Paths.shellCommand)
- `startCommand` (readonly string): Starting it: -n (--no-duplicate) exits at once if axiom already runs, so a second autostart line or a reloaded hyprland.lua can't start another copy
- `notIncludedProblem` (readonly string): Why a file mode isn't in effect (CompositorConfigManager.problem)
- `notManagedProblem` (readonly string)
- `blockedProblem` (readonly string)
- `emptyModuleText` (readonly string): The included module once axiom isn't in that mode (every part a no-op)
- `inputsKey` (readonly string): Everything else the layer is made of (CompositorConfigManager re-applies the layer when it changes)
- `liveLinesHook` (var): CompositorConfigManager's: the live lines, noting which parts they apply.

### Signals

- `claimed(string adopted)`: The takeover of hyprland.lua is done (`adopted`: the file name the previous one went to in user/, or "")
- `blocked()`: It won't take over (blockedProblem)
- `released(string result)`: Leaving managed is done: "restored" | "written" | …
- `bindsMerged(var binds)`: The binds a merge moved in for good

### Functions

- `isComplete(bind)`: Whether a configured bind has everything it needs to be bound
- `moduleText(spec)`: The included file, from `spec` (CompositorConfigManager.spec(true)): a module whose setup() applies what's enabled
- `managedText(spec)`: The managed hyprland.lua, from `spec` as for moduleText
- `releasedText(mode)`: The hyprland.lua leaving managed gives back when the takeover set nothing aside (claim_hyprland.sh release), starting axiom (and loading its module in included mode)
- `liveLines(spec)`: The look, the input and the blur as Lua lines evaluated now, from `spec` (CompositorConfigManager.spec(false))
- `runLive(lines)`: Evaluates `lines` now, then reads the options back (gapsOut)
- `setCursor(theme, size)`
- `runtimeApply()`: The runtime layer (detached, and the fallback of the file modes)
- `runtimeClear()`: Takes the runtime layer's binds out (the file is loaded now)
- `noteReload()`: Hyprland reloaded its config, dropping the runtime layer
- `checkLoaded(callback)`: Calls back with whether the file is in effect: Hyprland answers "ok" when the file's marker is set in its Lua state
- `reload(callback)`: Reloads Hyprland's config (it doesn't watch files a config loads)
- `checkManaged(callback)`: `callback` (optional) gets managedCheck once known
- `claim()`
- `release()`
- `findMonitorConflicts()`
- `clearConflicts()`
- `mergeUserBinds(only)`: `only`: one file name in user/ (the adopted one), else all of them
- `previewMerge()`: Counts what a Merge would move, changing nothing (`mergeable`)
